info.title: Juiced API
info.description: API for submitting pings and leads to Juiced. Build on the v1 endpoints under `/v1`. The unversioned `/ping` and `/leads` endpoints are the frozen legacy contract and are deprecated.

post.description:
Submits partial lead data to check for matching bids before sending the full lead. Use it to see pricing and availability before you commit to a full lead submission.

The response depends on your source type.
- **Vendor sources** receive a single `price`, never the bids behind it.
- **Every other source** receives the matching `bids`, each with the buyer's name for TCPA consent.

Every ping that passes validation returns `200`, whatever its `status`. Keep the returned `id` and send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

200.description: Ping evaluated. Check `data.status` for the outcome.

matchedWithoutBidder.summary: Matched with no bidder (marketplace or Club)

post.description:
Submits a complete lead for processing. The lead is validated, checked for duplicates, matched to a lead type, and distributed to a buyer (or placed in the marketplace or Club).

If you pinged first, include the ping's `id` as `ping_id`. You can also echo the `bids[].id` you chose as `bid_id`; it is checked but doesn't change who gets the lead.

Send a `transaction_id` so a retry can never create a second lead. One `transaction_id` is one lead on either API version.

201.description: Lead received. Check `data.status` for the outcome. A retry with the same `transaction_id` and payload returns this same response again.

409.description: The `transaction_id` was already used and this request can't be replayed.

Retry-After.description: Sent with `idempotency_in_progress` only. Seconds to wait before retrying the same request.

post.description:
**Deprecated.** This is the frozen legacy contract. Build new integrations on [`POST /v1/ping`](/api-reference/endpoint/v1/ping). Every response carries a `Deprecation` header and a `Link` header pointing to the v1 endpoint.

The response has one of two shapes.
- **Bids** has `ping_id`, `message` and `bids`. Non-vendor sources get it when the ping went through matching, and for test-mode zips.
- **Price** has `message`, `price` and `ping_id`. Vendor sources always get it, and so does any ping answered before matching (duplicate, quota reached, or rejected).

PartnerIdHeader.name: X-Partner-Id
PartnerIdHeader.description: Public ID of the partner you're pinging on behalf of. The ping is recorded against that partner when the partner is linked to the source whose credentials you use. Optional but recommended for any partner-mediated integration.

XRequestId.description: Unique ID for this request, sent on every v1 response (errors included). Quote it when contacting support.

Deprecation.description: Marks the legacy endpoint as deprecated (RFC 9745). The value is `@` followed by the Unix timestamp of the deprecation date.

SuccessorLink.description: Points to the v1 endpoint that replaces this one.

Basic Auth.description: Use your source's API key as the username and API secret as the password. Base64 encode the credentials in the format `api_key:api_secret`.

Bearer Token.description: Use a bearer token generated for your source.

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category. Only fields marked required for ping must be sent.

transaction_id.description: Your own ID for this lead, such as an order or lead number. A retry with the same `transaction_id` and payload returns the original response instead of creating a second lead. Numbers are accepted and treated as strings.

ping_id.description: The `id` returned by `POST /v1/ping`. Links this lead to the ping's match and pricing. A legacy ping UUID is rejected.

bid_id.description: Any `bids[].id` returned by `POST /v1/ping` for your account. It is checked but doesn't change who gets the lead.

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category.

id.description: The ping's ID. Send it as `ping_id` when you post the lead.

status.description: How the ping was answered. `matched` means a buyer (or the marketplace or Club) will take the lead. `no_match` means nobody will, including when the source has reached a lead quota. `duplicate` means it matched a duplicate check. `rejected` means it was refused before matching.

price.description: Vendor sources only. The price offered for the lead, in dollars. `0` when there's no match.

bids.description: Every source except vendors. The bids behind the answer. Empty when there's no match.

reason.description: Only on a ping rejected by the distribution loop guard, because the ping already passed through this account or exceeded the hop limit.

id.description: The bid's ID. It's a `bid_…` for a customer bid, the partner's `prt_…` for a partner, or the ping's own `ping_…` when the match has no bidder behind it (marketplace or Club). Echo it as `bid_id` when you post the lead.

price.description: Price offered for the lead, in dollars.

tcpa_name.description: Buyer name to use in TCPA consent language.

customer_id.description: Present when a customer placed the bid. The customer's public ID.

partner_id.description: Present when a partner made the offer. The partner's public ID.

status.description: The outcome, decided by the source's status response mapping. By default, `accepted` covers leads that were assigned, posted to a partner, placed on the marketplace or parked in the Club; `rejected` covers Unassigned, Audit and Uncategorized leads; `duplicate` covers duplicates.

price.description: What the source earns for the lead, in dollars. Always `0` unless `status` is `accepted`.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Branch on this, not on `message`.

errors.description: Only with `validation_failed`. Messages keyed by field.

lead_id.description: Only with `idempotency_version_mismatch`. The lead the `transaction_id` already created.

transaction_id.description: Your own ID for this lead, such as an order or lead number. A retry with the same `transaction_id` and payload returns the original response instead of creating a second lead. Numbers are accepted and treated as strings.

ping_id.description: The `ping_id` returned by the ping (a UUID), or the ping's `ping_…` public ID.

bid_id.description: A bid `id` from the ping response. It must be a UUID, so a partner's numeric bid `id` can't be echoed. It doesn't change who gets the lead.

zip.description: Postal code. Must be valid for your account's operating countries. With the source in test mode, zips `00001` to `00005` return fixed outcomes.

additionalProperties.description: Additional fields as configured for your source and lead category.
